title: DRE profiles
description: Connections and destinations, in `profiles.yml`: what reports read from and where outputs go. Kept outside the project (`~/.dre`, `--profiles-dir` or `DRE_PROFILES_DIR`). Every profile lists its targets (environments). Each profile the run uses picks one: `--target`, else `DRE_TARGET` (either sets every profile), else the profile's own `target`, else `dev`; a used profile without that entry is an error.

connections.description: Database connections, referenced by `default_profile`, `profile:` (report, query, Set, folder `+profile`) and a source's `profile`.

sources.description: DRE 0.1's name for `connections:`. Still read in 0.2.x, with a warning: rename it to `connections:`.

connection.description: A named connection with one entry per target (environment).

target.description: This profile's entry when neither `--target` nor `DRE_TARGET` is set (dbt's key). Default: `dev`. It doesn't change `target.name`, the run's target.

targets.description: The environments of this connection, by name (e.g. `dev`, `prod`).

destination.description: A named destination with one entry per target (environment).

targets.description: The environments of this destination, by name (e.g. `dev`, `prod`). An entry is a delivery configuration, or `{deliver: false}` to deliver nowhere on that target.

target.description: This profile's entry when neither `--target` nor `DRE_TARGET` is set (dbt's key). Default: `dev`. It doesn't change `target.name`, the run's target.

One target of a profile: a connection or delivery configuration. `type` names the plugin; every other key is a field of that plugin (see the plugins reference), and secrets belong in `{{ env_var('NAME') }}`.

type.description: The plugin type of the connection, e.g. `duckdb`, `postgres`, `databricks`, `sftp`, `s3`. `local` needs no plugin.

no_delivery.description: A destination entry is a delivery configuration (`type` and the plugin's fields, as for a connection), or `{deliver: false}`: it deliberately delivers nowhere. The output stays in the target path, the run logs it, and `run_results.json` records the delivery as `not_delivered`. Destinations only.

deliver.description: `false`: this target delivers nowhere. Takes no other keys.
